newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israel frees two Lebanese civilians.
newsitem.headline: Israel frees two Lebanese civilians.

text.p: Israeli forces have freed two Lebanese civilians detained in south Lebanon last month, pro-Israeli militia sources said on Wednesday.
They said Joseph Nahra and his cousin Jean Nahra were released on Sunday after being detained since July 3.
Joseph and his two brothers -- Lebanese journalist Roger and retired policeman Michel -- were arrested along with their cousin Jean, a merchant, last month.

Roger was freed on August 6. He said at the time that he, his brothers and cousin were taken to Khiam detention centre, run by the pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) in a security zone Israel occupies in south Lebanon.
Michel Nahra, 47, remains in detention, the London-based Amnesty International said in a press statement faxed to Reuters in Beirut.
"Amnesty International remains concerned for his well-being and therefore action on his behalf should continue," the group said.
Israel holds a 15-km (nine-mile)-wide border zone in south Lebanon. Pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas are fighting to oust Israeli troops and their local militia allies from the zone.
